sentences.en: Hello and welcome to The Rest Is History.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《余韵皆史》。

sentences.en: Today we're tackling one of the big beasts of historical arguments, the kind of subject that frankly is likely to get us cancelled.
sentences.zh: 今天我们将探讨历史论战中的一个庞然大物，这种话题坦率地说，很可能会让我们遭到“取消”。

sentences.en: We're going to be talking about empire.
sentences.zh: 我们要谈论的是帝国。

sentences.en: What is empire?
sentences.zh: 什么是帝国？

sentences.en: What's it for?
sentences.zh: 帝国有什么用？

sentences.en: Where's it come from?
sentences.zh: 帝国从何而来？

sentences.en: And can it ever be a good thing?
sentences.zh: 帝国可能是一件好事吗？

sentences.en: Or is it always morally wrong?
sentences.zh: 还是说它在道德上总是错误的？

sentences.en: Tom Holland, I've been dreaming since we started of getting you cancelled and this is my chance.
sentences.zh: 汤姆·霍兰，从节目一开始我就梦想着看你被“取消”，现在这就是我的机会了。

sentences.en: So let's start by saying what we are going to talk about.
sentences.zh: 所以，让我们先说说我们要讨论的内容。

sentences.en: That's a vote for confidence.
sentences.zh: 这可真投了信任票啊。

sentences.en: Yeah, of course.
sentences.zh: 对，当然。

sentences.en: We're talking about empires very broadly, aren't we?
sentences.zh: 我们是在一个非常广泛的层面上讨论帝国，对吧？

sentences.en: We're not going to be talking about a specific empire.
sentences.zh: 我们不打算讨论某一个具体的帝国。

sentences.en: We're going to span the whole of history and the idea.
sentences.zh: 我们要跨越整个历史和这一概念本身。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, let's get down to it.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我的意思是，我们言归正传吧。

sentences.en: What is an empire, would you say?
sentences.zh: 依你之见，什么是帝国？

sentences.en: Well, let's go to the etymology.
sentences.zh: 好吧，让我们从词源说起。

sentences.en: Let's say, you know, where does the word empire come from?
sentences.zh: 比方说，你知道，“帝国”这个词是从哪里来的？

sentences.en: It comes from a Latin word, imperium.
sentences.zh: 它来自一个拉丁词：imperium。

sentences.en: And the meaning of imperium over the course of the Roman Empire changes in a quite interesting way.
sentences.zh: 在罗马帝国期间，imperium 的含义经历了一种非常有趣的变化。

sentences.en: So imperium is, it's a command, but it's also the right that someone has to issue a command.
sentences.zh: 所以，imperium 既是一个命令，也是某人发号施令的权力。

sentences.en: So an imperator.
sentences.zh: 因此就有了 imperator（统帅）。

sentences.en: It's like authority almoSt.
sentences.zh: 它几乎就像是权威。

sentences.en: So an imperator, conventionally translated as a general, is someone who has authority, who has power over the men who are subject to him.
sentences.zh: 因此，通常被翻译为将军的 imperator，是指拥有权威、对受其支配的人拥有权力的某个人。

sentences.en: Imperator becomes the title that Augustus, the first Roman emperor, gets.
sentences.zh: Imperator 成为了罗马第一位皇帝奥古斯都获得的头衔。

sentences.en: And our word emperor comes from imperator.
sentences.zh: 我们所用的“皇帝”（emperor）一词就源于 imperator。

sentences.en: And so it implies that he has imperium over a vast sway of the empire and of the people within it.
sentences.zh: 因此它暗示着他对帝国的大片领土以及其中的人民拥有 imperium（统治权）。

sentences.en: And it's during Augustus's life that a great map of the empire goes up in the forum.
sentences.zh: 正是在奥古斯都在世期间，广场上竖起了一张帝国的巨大地图。

sentences.en: And that starts to, that's a kind of a symbol for the way in which the understanding of imperium changes to actually mean the physical territory that the Romans have power over.
sentences.zh: 这开始成为一种象征，标志着对 imperium 的理解转变为实际上指罗马人拥有权力的物理领土。

sentences.en: And I think, and I think that that sense of a physical amount of territory, you know, in the Roman classically, it's, it's kind of subcontinental.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，而且我认为那种实体领土的概念，你知道，在罗马的经典定义中，它有点像次大陆级别的。

sentences.en: It's a vast, vast array of territory combined with authority that, that one person or perhaps, you know, a particular people have authority and power over other peoples.
sentences.zh: 它是大量领土的结合，并伴随着一个人或者也许是一个特定的人群对其他人拥有的权威和权力。

sentences.en: So I think that the, the, perhaps the two key elements of empire are that you have a center,
sentences.zh: 所以我想，帝国的两个核心要素可能在于：你拥有一个中心，

sentences.en: you have a dominant center and you have peripheral, yeah, you have, you have a metropole and then you have peripheral regions.
sentences.zh: 你拥有一个占据统治地位的中心，并且你拥有外围，对，你拥有一个核心都市，然后你拥有外围地区。

sentences.en: And also you have an idea that, that, that one, you know, that this, this, this metropolis, this metropole, this center has authority and power over the peripheral regions.
sentences.zh: 并且你还有一个观念，即这个首都、这个核心都市、这个中心对周边地区拥有权威和权力。

sentences.en: So I would guess that would be how I would describe empires.
sentences.zh: 所以我想这大概就是我描述帝国的方式。

sentences.en: But, but Tom, could you not go, I mean, I don't want to play the whole fixture on away turf
sentences.zh: 但是，汤姆，难道你就不能——我的意思是，我不想在客场作战，

sentences.en: as it were, we should come further forward at some point, but couldn't you go further back
sentences.zh: 就像这样，我们在某个时候应该把话题推进到现在，但难道你不能追溯得更远，

sentences.en: and say that the very first civilizations that we know of, let's say, you know, 5,000 years ago or whatever, that the two kingdoms of Egypt, the Indus Valley, sort of Mesopotamia,
sentences.zh: 并指出我们所知的最早的文明，比方说，你知道的，五千年前左右，埃及的两个王国、印度河流域、美索不达米亚那种地方，

sentences.en: the Akkad and all these kinds of places, that, that society itself originated often as empires.
sentences.zh: 阿卡德以及所有这些地方，社会本身往往就是作为帝国起源的？

sentences.en: I mean, obviously it didn't originate as nation states.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，显然它并不是作为民族国家起源的。

sentences.en: Well, yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的。

sentences.en: Sophisticated powers had elites that, that governed places with lots of different people who often spoke different dialects or languages or maybe worshiped different gods and that
sentences.zh: 成熟的政权拥有精英阶层，他们统治着许多不同的人群，这些人通常说不同的方言或语言，或者可能崇拜不同的神明，而

sentences.en: they had a single authority.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有单一的权威。

sentences.en: I mean, obviously Persia is the, is the famous example of that, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，显然波斯就是这方面的著名例子，不是吗？

sentences.en: Well, there's this fantastic phrase, imperiogenesis, the process by which empires come to be formed.
sentences.zh: 这里有一个极妙的词，imperiogenesis，即帝国形成的过程。

sentences.en: And you talked about Egypt and you talked about Mesopotamia.
sentences.zh: 你谈到了埃及，也谈到了美索不达米亚。

sentences.en: In Egypt, the figure of the Pharaoh, he's a figure within, in the Roman sense, imperium.
sentences.zh: 在埃及，法老这个人物，在罗马的意义上，他是一个拥有 imperium 的人物。

sentences.en: He has power, but he also has, comes to have authority over the entire Nile Valley that comes to constitute the kingdom of Egypt.
sentences.zh: 他拥有权力，但他也逐渐对构成埃及王国的整个尼罗河流域拥有了权威。

sentences.en: And everyone who lives along the Nile, they speak the same language, they essentially worship the same gods, they acknowledge the same ruler.
sentences.zh: 所有沿着尼罗河居住的人，他们说同样的语言，基本上崇拜同样的神明，他们承认同一个统治者。

sentences.en: And so in a, I guess that ancient Egypt approximates perhaps more closely to our sense of a nation state.
sentences.zh: 所以在某种程度上，我猜古埃及可能更接近我们对民族国家的理解。

sentences.en: In Mesopotamia, you have different cities and each city has to build walls, essentially because to keep the wealth within and to keep outsiders outside.
sentences.zh: 在美索不达米亚，你拥有不同的城市，每个城市都必须修建城墙，主要是为了把财富留在里面，把外人挡在外面。

sentences.en: And Mesopotamia, on top of that, has to deal with the fact that beyond the floodplains of
sentences.zh: 不仅如此，美索不达米亚还必须面对这样一个现实：在底格里斯河和幼发拉底河的冲击平原之外，

sentences.en: the Tigris and the Euphrates, you have predatory powers lurking in the mountains, perhaps lurking
sentences.zh: 潜伏着山中的掠夺性势力，或许也潜伏在沙漠中，他们

sentences.en: in the deserts, who would, you know, if they had the chance, would come and grab a bit of this.
sentences.zh: 只要有机会，就会跑来抢夺这里的一切。

sentences.en: So you cannot survive as a city-state in Mesopotamia unless you have a degree of militarism.
sentences.zh: 因此，除非你具备一定程度的军国主义，否则你无法在美索不达米亚作为城邦生存下去。

sentences.en: And this militarism, in turn, inevitably fosters an ambition.
sentences.zh: 而这种军国主义反过来又不可避免地助长了一种野心。

sentences.en: Famously, the first person to do it, supposedly, is this guy Sargon of the city of Akkad, who starts to conquer other cities.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，据称第一个这么做的人是来自阿卡德城的萨尔贡，他开始征服其他城市。

sentences.en: And so it's the tradition of imperialism in the Middle East, really, I think, that is the kind of the great granddaddy of what today we would think of as empires.
sentences.zh: 因此，中东的帝国主义传统，实际上，我认为这就是我们今天所理解的帝国的伟大鼻祖。

sentences.en: Because what begins with Akkad goes on, you get Assyria, you get Babylon.
sentences.zh: 因为从阿卡德开始，延续下去，你有了亚述，你有了巴比伦。

sentences.en: Assyria is a famously brutal and predatory empire.
sentences.zh: 亚述是一个以残暴和掠夺闻名的帝国。

sentences.en: And essentially, its rule is founded on military oppression and on terror.
sentences.zh: 从根本上说，它的统治建立在军事压迫和恐怖之上。

sentences.en: So when the Assyrians conquer a rival people, they will deport them.
sentences.zh: 所以当亚述人征服敌对民族时，他们会将其流放。

sentences.en: Famously, they do this to the 10 tribes of Israel.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，他们对以色列的十个部落就是这样做的。

sentences.en: And in time over the course of the Assyrian Empire, people who are deported to Assyria come to be called booty.
sentences.zh: 随着亚述帝国的推移，被流放到亚述的人最终被称为战利品。

sentences.en: So they are, you know, part of the loot that the Assyrians are carrying off.
sentences.zh: 所以他们，你知道的，是亚述人劫掠的财物的一部分。

sentences.en: Those who resist are kind of ritually and humiliatingly killed.
sentences.zh: 那些反抗的人会被以一种充满仪式感且羞辱性的方式杀死。

sentences.en: People are, you know, leaders are transported back, put in cages with wild animals outside the cities of Assyria so that people can watch them.
sentences.zh: 人们，你知道的，领袖们会被运回来，关在亚述城市外的野生动物铁笼里，供人们观看。

sentences.en: Other people, you know, the kings have their heads cut off.
sentences.zh: 其他人，你知道的，国王会被砍头。

sentences.en: The royal families will have their heads cut off.
sentences.zh: 王室成员会被砍头。

sentences.en: Courtiers will be brought back to Nineveh, made to parade through the streets with the heads around their necks.
sentences.zh: 朝臣会被带回尼尼微，被迫脖子上挂着人头游街示众。

sentences.en: So these are spectacles of dread and terror.
sentences.zh: 所以这些都是恐惧与恐怖的奇观。

sentences.en: Assyria ends up basically being wiped from the face of the earth.
sentences.zh: 亚述最终基本上被从地球上抹去了。

sentences.en: Nineveh gets trampled down.
sentences.zh: 尼尼微被夷为平地。

sentences.en: And the reason for that is that terror and dread in the long run is insufficient to keep an empire.
sentences.zh: 原因在于，长远来看，恐怖和惊恐不足以维持一个帝国。

sentences.en: And the great empire that emerges, which, you know, expands far beyond Mesopotamia to rule
sentences.zh: 而随之崛起并将其版图远远扩展到美索不达米亚之外、统治了

sentences.en: Egypt and all the way to the Indus, is, as you said, the Persian Empire.
sentences.zh: 埃及一直到印度河的伟大帝国，正如你所说，就是波斯帝国。

sentences.en: And the great thing that the Persians innovate is that they identify their empire with moral virtue.
sentences.zh: 波斯人的一大创新在于，他们将自己的帝国与美德等同起来。

sentences.en: Their empire is a force for truth, is a force for light, is a force for goodness.
sentences.zh: 他们的帝国是真理的力量，是光明的力量，是善良的力量。

sentences.en: And by defining their empire in that sense, it immediately means that those who oppose them are on the side of darkness and the lie.
sentences.zh: 通过这种方式来定义他们的帝国，就意味着那些反对他们的人立刻就站在了黑暗和谎言的一边。

sentences.en: But so, Tom, I mean, you obviously emphasise violence.
sentences.zh: 但是，汤姆，我的意思是，你显然强调了暴力。

sentences.en: And I guess a lot of, you know, 21st century scholars and people who sort of think about empire think of empires in terms of violence and power and all this sort of oppression, I
sentences.zh: 我想许多21世纪的学者以及思考帝国的人，倾向于从暴力、权力和所有这些压迫的角度来思考帝国，我

sentences.en: suppose.
sentences.zh: 想是的。

sentences.en: But there is obviously another way to think about this, which is that, let's say, Persia, you give the example of Persia.
sentences.zh: 但显然还有另一种思考方式，那就是，比方说波斯，你举了波斯的例子。

sentences.en: I know you've written about this in your book, Persian Fire.
sentences.zh: 我知道你在你的书《波斯之火》中写过这一点。

sentences.en: So the Persians have, you know, this amazing network of roads.
sentences.zh: 所以波斯人拥有，你知道的，这个惊人的公路网。

sentences.en: They've got weights and measures.
sentences.zh: 他们有度量衡。

sentences.en: They've got a currency.
sentences.zh: 他们有货币。

sentences.en: They've got a sense of, you know, they view their own world as this kind of walled garden, don't they?
sentences.zh: 他们有一种观念，你知道的，他们将自己的世界视为一个围墙花园，不是吗？

sentences.en: And beyond is kind of barbarism and savagery and within all is order.
sentences.zh: 而外界则是野蛮与粗野，内部则是一片秩序。

sentences.en: And presumably you could make an argument that if you're a sort of, you know, Joe Bloggs from media or from, you know, Mesopotamia or what's now Iran, you might think, well, you
sentences.zh: 据此你可能会提出这样一个论点：如果你是来自米底或美索不达米亚，或者现在的伊朗的一个普通人（Joe Bloggs），你可能会想，

sentences.en: know, life isn't actually so bad in the heart of this empire.
sentences.zh: 在这个帝国的腹地，生活其实并没有那么糟糕。

sentences.en: We've got all this infrastructure, we've got all this stuff.
sentences.zh: 我们拥有这一切基础设施，我们拥有一切物资。

sentences.en: Of course, there is always the ubiquitous threat that I might get my head cut off or whatever,
sentences.zh: 当然，始终存在着我可能会被砍头诸如此类的无处不在的威胁，

sentences.en: but I'd rather that than live in an anarchic world of sort of savage clans fighting each other all the time and invaders coming and going and a sort of Hobbesian struggle for
sentences.zh: 但我宁愿这样，也不愿生活在一个野蛮部落无休止相互厮杀、侵略者络绎不绝、充满霍布斯式

sentences.en: existence.
sentences.zh: 生存斗争的无政府世界里。

sentences.en: I mean, that's the justification for empire through history, isn't it, that it equates to order?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就是历史上帝国存在的正当理由，不是吗？它等同于秩序。

sentences.en: Well, well, I suppose that the Near East has basically always been ruled by empires, pretty much from, you know, from the time of Sargon of Akkad.
sentences.zh: 嗯，嗯，我想近东基本上一直都是由帝国统治的，几乎从阿卡德人萨尔贡的时代开始就是如此。

sentences.en: And the earliest experience of empire, by and large, is terrible.
sentences.zh: 而且人们对帝国的早期体验总体而言是可怕的。

sentences.en: And the famous, you know, I mean, seismically influential articulation of this is what we call the Old Testament, because the Israelites and then the people of Judah, the southern
sentences.zh: 而众所周知的、具有震荡般深远影响的对这一体验的表达就是我们所说的《旧约》，因为以色列人，然后是南方的犹大

sentences.en: kingdom, are, you know, they're tiny, they're small, they're minnows.
sentences.zh: 王国的国民，你知道的，他们非常微小，他们很弱小。

sentences.en: And so they're always being trampled down by the big powers, by the Egyptians, by the
sentences.zh: 所以他们总是被大国、被埃及人、被

sentences.en: Babylonians, by the Assyrians.
sentences.zh: 巴比伦人、被亚述人践踏。

sentences.en: And pharaohs and kings of Assyria in the Old Testament are sinister figures.
sentences.zh: 在《旧约》中，法老和亚述国王都是阴险的人物。

sentences.en: There is one exception that proves, and this exception is Cyrus, who is hailed by Isaiah as the Messiah, as the anointed one, God's agent.
sentences.zh: 有一个例外证明了这一点，这个例外就是居鲁士，他被以赛亚尊为弥赛亚，尊为受膏者、上帝的代理人。

sentences.en: Because Cyrus the Great, what Cyrus does is to say to the deported peoples who've been carried to Mesopotamia, you can go back home.
sentences.zh: 因为居鲁士大帝，居鲁士所做的是对那些被掳到美索不达米亚的被流放者说，你们可以回家了。

sentences.en: And among those are the people who will become the Jews, who go back, you know, they've been weeping by the rivers of Babylon.
sentences.zh: 在这其中就包括那些后来成为犹太人的人，他们回去了，你知道的，他们曾坐在巴比伦河畔哭泣。

sentences.en: They go back to Jerusalem and they refound it.
sentences.zh: 他们回到了耶路撒冷并将其重建。

sentences.en: And so the Persians in the biblical tradition are remembered as good guys.
sentences.zh: 因此在圣经传统中，波斯人被铭记为好人。

sentences.en: And absolutely, they, you know, for the people who become the Jews, the Persians are remembered
sentences.zh: 而且绝对地，对于那些后来成为犹太人的人来说，他们对波斯人的记忆

sentences.en: very, very fondly because basically they, you know, they provide peace, they provide order,
sentences.zh: 非常非常美好，因为基本上他们，你知道的，他们带来了和平，他们带来了秩序，

sentences.en: they allow them, they allow the people to, the people of Jerusalem to rebuild the temple.
sentences.zh: 他们允许，他们允许耶路撒冷的人民重建圣殿。

sentences.en: But isn't that how a lot of people living in the Persian Empire would have thought of Persia?
sentences.zh: 但生活在波斯帝国的许多人难道不正是这样看待波斯的吗？

sentences.en: Let's say, for example, the classic thing we talked in previous podcasts about Alexander the Great.
sentences.zh: 比方说，我们在之前的播客中讨论过亚历山大大帝的经典案例。

sentences.en: Alexander the Great invades Persia and he says he's coming as a liberator and a hero.
sentences.zh: 亚历山大大帝入侵波斯，他说自己是以解放者和英雄的身份前来的。

sentences.en: And his story in the West is always told of this intrepid adventurer who goes into this sort of evil empire and cuts a swathe through it.
sentences.zh: 他在西方的故事总是被讲述为一个无畏的冒险家，深入这个邪恶的帝国并横扫千军。

sentences.en: But presumably if you're, you know, Joe Bloggs living in Persia and this Macedonian turns up with his army and says, I'm going to tear down your empire, I'm coming as a liberator.
sentences.zh: 但假设如果你是一个生活在波斯的普通人（Joe Bloggs），这个马其顿人带着他的军队出现，并说我要摧毁你们的帝国，我是作为解放者而来的。

sentences.en: I mean, it's a nightmare, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这简直是一场噩梦，不是吗？

sentences.en: These people kind of who don't speak your language, kind of charging through your country, smashing everything up.
sentences.zh: 这些说着你听不懂语言的人，在你的国家横冲直撞，砸毁一切。

sentences.en: Presumably a lot of people quite like living in the Persian Empire.

sentences.zh: 所以他把话塞进那些抵抗罗马人的蛮族口中，他让一个苏格兰首领说出了那句名言：

sentences.zh: 现在我们要探讨一些关于帝国的问题。

sentences.en: And now we're going to get into some of these questions about empire.
sentences.zh: 但在我们开始之前，汤姆，你还没有真正回答那个重大问题，那就是：帝国总是坏的吗？

sentences.zh: 所以……

sentences.en: So...

sentences.zh: 我觉得这很不负责任。

sentences.zh: 这非常避重就轻。

sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 邪恶的帝国？

sentences.en: Bad empire?
sentences.zh: 肯定不是。

sentences.en: Surely not.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以阿拉伯……

sentences.en: Well, so the Arab...
sentences.zh: 你不会要持这种观点吧。

sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这难道不像是对你来说合理的论点吗？

sentences.zh: 我最近和某人争论过这个问题，他们说，你知道的，帝国总是坏的，它们总是压迫性的，诸如此类。

sentences.en: I had this argument with somebody recently and they said, you know, empires are always bad, they're always oppressive and all the rest of it.
sentences.zh: 然后我说，当然，当人们进行这种对话时，他们几乎总是想到18、19世纪和20世纪初的欧洲殖民帝国，

sentences.en: And I said, and of course, when people have this conversation, they're almost always thinking about European colonial empires of the 18th, 19th and early 20th centuries,
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: aren't they?
sentences.zh: 然后我说，哦，奥斯曼帝国是一件非常糟糕的事情吗？

sentences.en: And I said, oh, the Ottoman empire, a really bad thing?
sentences.zh: 然后出现了一段尴尬的沉默，不知道该说什么。

sentences.en: And there was this sort of embarrassed pause, didn't know what to say.
sentences.zh: 接着我说，就像你刚才说的那样，阿拉伯帝国。

sentences.en: And then I said, exactly what you said, the Arab empire.
sentences.zh: 你打算争辩说阿拉伯帝国是邪恶的吗？

sentences.en: Are you going to argue that the Arab empire was evil?
sentences.zh: 当然，没有人会提出这种争论，不是因为他们，我认为是因为他们害怕，而是因为这是一种不言自明的愚蠢说法，

sentences.en: And of course, nobody will make that argument, not because they, I think because they're afraid, but because it's a self-evidently foolish thing to say,
sentences.zh: 去审视一个持续了几个世纪、绝大多数人视为理所当然的事物，却只是用这种简单化的方式一笔带过，我认为简直荒谬至极。

sentences.en: to look at something that lasted centuries, that most of its people took completely for granted, and to just sort of write it off in this simplistic way, I think is just bizarre.
sentences.zh: 毫无道理。

sentences.en: And very similarly, the Romans, the Romeoi of Constantinople, when they're fighting to keep their city and their empire against the Ottomans,
sentences.zh: 而且非常相似的是，罗马人，也就是君士坦丁堡的罗马人，当他们在与奥斯曼帝国作战以保卫自己的城市和帝国时，

sentences.en: you know, they're doing it as Romans.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们是以罗马人的身份在这样做。

sentences.en: Are they, they see that likewise?
sentences.zh: 是吗，他们也是这么看的吗？

sentences.en: There were the battles there.
sentences.zh: 当时那里发生过战役。

sentences.en: Yeah, but they, you know, they, these are people who were conquered very brutally by the Romans back in the second, first century BC.
sentences.zh: 对，但他们，你知道，他们，这些人早在公元前二、一世纪就被罗马人非常残酷地征服了。

sentences.en: And by the 15th century, they are identifying the fact that they are Roman with God's purpose.
sentences.zh: 到了十五世纪，他们把自己的罗马身份认同与上帝的意志联系在了一起。

sentences.en: So in that, you know, who are we to say the Byzantine empire was, was, was evil?
sentences.zh: 所以在这个意义上，你知道，我们算什么，怎么能说拜占庭帝国是邪恶的呢？

sentences.en: Well, I mean, also, isn't it just the case that basically, I mean, John Darwin, a historian at Oxford, makes this point in his book, After Tamerlane,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，还有，难道不是这样的吗，基本上，我是说，牛津大学的历史学家约翰·达尔文在他关于帝国的伟大著作《帖木儿之后》中，

sentences.en: which is a great history of empires.
sentences.zh: 提出了这样一个观点。

sentences.en: And he basically says, empire is the natural unit.
sentences.zh: 他基本上说，帝国是自然的单位。

sentences.en: For most of history, empire has been the natural unit of human organisation.
sentences.zh: 在人类历史的大部分时间里，帝国一直是人类组织的基本单位。

sentences.en: The more powerful you are, the richer you are, the more likely you are to have an empire.
sentences.zh: 你越强大，越富有，你就越有可能拥有一个帝国。

sentences.en: The Venetians had an empire.
sentences.zh: 威尼斯人曾拥有一个帝国。

sentences.en: You know, Portugal had an empire.
sentences.zh: 你知道，葡萄牙曾拥有一个帝国。

sentences.en: Belgium had an empire.
sentences.zh: 比利时曾拥有一个帝国。

sentences.en: Basically, whenever you're at the top of the tree, you have an empire because it's an expression of influence and authority and all of those kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 基本上，每当你登上权力之巅，你就会拥有一个帝国，因为它是影响力和权威以及所有诸如此类事物的体现。

sentences.en: And a world without empires would be a world without human beings.
sentences.zh: 一个没有帝国的世界将是一个没有人类的世界。

sentences.en: I mean, that would be my view, because I don't think you can fragment the world into, into sort of happy, harmonious, democratic nation states.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这会是我的观点，因为我不认为你能把世界碎片化成那种快乐、和谐、民主的民族国家。

sentences.en: It just doesn't work that way.
sentences.zh: 事情根本不是那样运作的。

sentences.en: Well, I'm not sure I agree with that, because the John Darwin book, After Tamerlane, is basically focused on Eurasia.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我不太确定我是否同意这一点，因为约翰·达尔文的书《帖木儿之后》主要聚焦于欧亚大陆。

sentences.en: And so it's focused on areas where huge empires absolutely are the norm.
sentences.zh: 所以它聚焦于那些庞大帝国绝对是常态的地区。

sentences.en: So Persian Empire, Ottoman Empire, Chinese Empire, the various empires of the Silk Road that kind of rise and fall.
sentences.zh: 比如波斯帝国、奥斯曼帝国、中国帝国，以及丝绸之路上各种兴衰交替的帝国。

sentences.en: But I do think Western Europe is different because I do think that it's, you know, we've already talked about this.
sentences.zh: 但我确实认为西欧是不同的，因为我觉得它，你知道的，我们之前已经讨论过这个了。

sentences.en: In the wake of the collapse of the Roman Empire in the West, a unitary power never really succeeds in establishing itself for a lengthy period of time in Western Europe.
sentences.zh: 在西罗马帝国崩溃之后，单一政权在西欧从未能真正成功地长期确立自己的统治。

sentences.en: And so for Europeans, the assumption is kind of hardwired that, as you say, that there should be a kind of patchwork of competing states.
sentences.zh: 因此对于欧洲人来说，内心的某种假设根深蒂固，正如你所说，应该存在一种相互竞争的国家的拼凑组合。

sentences.en: And yet, and yet they're trying to get, I mean, the Europeans have, the message you get from Europe now is that's the road to disaster and world war.
sentences.zh: 然而，然而他们现在正试图去，我是说，欧洲人，你现在从欧洲得到的信息是，那是通往灾难和世界大战的道路。

sentences.en: And, you know, Guy Verhofstadt, the sort of, who sees himself clearly as the kind of Count Cavour of European unification, the Belgian MEP, for me, the gift that keeps on giving.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，居伊·伏尔霍夫斯塔，这个自视为欧洲统一的加富尔伯爵之类的人，这位比利时欧洲议会议员，对我来说，真是个源源不断贡献笑料的人。

sentences.zh: 他说，你知道，欧洲应该是一个帝国。

sentences.en: We live in a world of empires and the European Union should be an empire.
sentences.zh: 我们生活在一个帝国的世界里，欧盟应该是一个帝国。

sentences.en: And we should put aside all these petty national differences.
sentences.zh: 我们应该抛开所有这些琐碎的国家分歧。

sentences.en: And that is the kind of assumption of the Treaty of Rome and European unification, right?
sentences.zh: 这就是《罗马条约》和欧洲统一的某种假定，对吧？

sentences.en: Ever closer union.
sentences.zh: 实现更加紧密的联盟。

sentences.en: So let's build an empire.
sentences.zh: 所以让我们建立一个帝国吧。

sentences.en: I think the processes within Europe that encourage, you know, states to fissure, attempts to construct European unity to fall apart,
sentences.zh: 我认为欧洲内部那些鼓励国家分裂、导致构建欧洲统一的尝试土崩瓦解的进程，

sentences.en: are as constant as the impulse to kind of bring them together.
sentences.zh: 与将它们凝聚在一起的冲动一样持久。

sentences.en: And there's never really been a kind of synergy.
sentences.zh: 而且从来没有真正产生过一种协同效应。

sentences.en: I mean, so this is the huge question for us now as Europeans is will the European hold together?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，所以对我们现代欧洲人来说，这是一个巨大的问题：欧洲能团结在一起吗？

sentences.en: You know, is it a kind of new order?
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是一种新秩序吗？

sentences.en: Has that age of fragmentation gone?
sentences.zh: 那个碎片化的时代已经过去了吗？

sentences.zh: 但矛盾的是，就在欧洲人试图这样做的同时，放眼全球，正如在联合国所反映的那样，

sentences.en: So the reason that the Middle East now is divided up into a patchwork of nations and is not an empire, basically for the first time since the Achaemenid era,

sentences.en: the first Persian empire, is because of European colonialism.
sentences.zh: 也就是第一个波斯帝国，原因正是欧洲殖民主义。

sentences.en: It's this fusion of biblical, classical traditions melded together.

sentences.zh: 在我看来，将某物去殖民化，基本上就是让它变得更西方化。

sentences.zh: 我觉得这是一个非常好的观点。

sentences.zh: 但同时我也认为，未来未必属于民族国家，因为当然，中国实际上就是一个帝国。

sentences.en: The United States, I would argue, is an empire.
sentences.zh: 我认为美国也是一个帝国。

sentences.en: Russia is an empire.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯是一个帝国。

sentences.en: So the idea that we're living in a post-imperial age, I think, is a fantasy.
sentences.zh: 所以我们生活在一个后帝国时代的想法，我认为是一种幻想。

sentences.zh: 不管怎样，我们完全没能进入问题环节。

sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: Do you want, well, I think, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 你想，好吧，我觉得，我不知道。

sentences.zh: 不，我的意思是，我对这件事的看法是，帝国前殖民地的人们其实根本不怎么去想大英帝国，

sentences.en: because they're too busy getting on with their lives.
sentences.zh: 因为他们太忙于过自己的生活了。

sentences.zh: 而我们听到声音的人，往往是那些过度政治化的人，或者对现在日益遥远的过去格外感兴趣的人。

sentences.en: I don't think the British are, if you look at recent polls, we're neither unusually proud nor unusually self-flagellating.
sentences.zh: 我不认为英国人，如果你看看最近的民调，我们既不是不寻常地骄傲，也不是不寻常地自我鞭笞。

sentences.en: It's the Dutch, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 是荷兰人吧？

sentences.en: The Dutch are kind of insanely proud of their empire.
sentences.zh: 荷兰人对他们的帝国有种疯狂的骄傲。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, I always think, you know, these polls are a bit ridiculous because I just don't think most people give a damn one way or the other.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我总是觉得，你知道，这些民调有点荒谬，因为我根本不认为大多数人会在乎到底是好是坏。

sentences.en: They don't think about it very much.
sentences.zh: 他们不怎么去想它。

sentences.en: There were brilliant surveys done in the mid-20th century, so around about the high point of their empire,
sentences.zh: 二十世纪中期曾做过非常出色的调查，大约是在他们帝国的鼎盛时期，

sentences.en: and they would ask people to name colonies or name possessions of the British Empire.
sentences.zh: 他们会让人说出大英帝国的殖民地或领地。

sentences.en: The most common one they knew people knew usually in was Scotland.
sentences.zh: 人们通常知道的最普遍的答案是苏格兰。

sentences.en: And I think something like Lincolnshire was in the top ten.
sentences.zh: 我想诸如林肯郡之类的名字都进了前十。

sentences.en: So that tells you how much people, I think, ever really cared about the British Empire or knew about it.
sentences.zh: 所以这说明了人们对大英帝国到底有多在乎，或者对它了解多少。

sentences.en: But there was a kind of vague, inchoate sense that it was a good thing, wasn't it?
sentences.zh: 但有一种模糊的、未成形的直觉，觉得这是一件好事，对吧？

sentences.en: Kind of lurking in the back of the mic.
sentences.zh: 潜藏在意识的深处。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think, see, my take on this, right, which we should get into in another podcast,
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为，看，我对此的看法是——我们应该在另一期播客中深入探讨——

sentences.en: is that people didn't give a damn about the empire, they liked being top nation, they liked status.
sentences.zh: 人们根本不在乎什么帝国，他们喜欢当头号大国，他们喜欢地位。

sentences.en: But whether that status involved a particular colony or, you know, control of a given sea lane or, I mean, they didn't know what was going on and they couldn't really care less.
sentences.zh: 但这种地位是否涉及某个特定的殖民地，或者，你知道的，对某条海上航线的控制，我是说，他们根本不知道发生了什么，也懒得去关心。

sentences.en: They just liked the impression of power and prestige.
sentences.zh: 他们只是喜欢权力和威望的印象。

sentences.en: I think that's what has always mattered to European colonialists.
sentences.zh: 我认为这才是欧洲殖民者一直以来所看重的。

sentences.en: And, of course, money.
sentences.zh: 当然，还有金钱。

sentences.en: Far more than the sort of, I don't think people ever obsessed about the nitty-gritty of their empires.
sentences.zh: 远胜于那种，我不认为人们曾经对帝国的繁文缛节或细枝末节着迷过。

sentences.en: But I think also running with that, right the way through the period of British imperial expansion and rule, is the sense that British people have that it's wrong.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，贯穿整个英国帝国扩张和统治时期的另一种感觉是，英国人有一种认为这是不对的意识。

sentences.en: So, always argument, always kind of anxiety about it.
sentences.zh: 所以，总是存在争论，总是伴随着某种焦虑。

sentences.en: And I think that, you know, that that is also part of what the British export.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，你知道，这也是英国人所输出的一部分内容。

sentences.en: So I was reading C.L.R.
sentences.zh: 所以我当时在读C·L·R·

sentences.en: James' book on cricket, Beyond the Boundary.
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯的板球著作《超越边界》。

sentences.en: And he's writing as a Marxist who's very, very anti-imperial.
sentences.zh: 他是作为一名非常坚定的反帝马克思主义者在写作。

sentences.en: And yet what's manifest is it's an incredibly British book.
sentences.zh: 然而显而易见的是，这是一本极其具有英国特色的书。

sentences.en: It's absolutely saturated in English literature and, you know, obsessed with cricket, with everything about it.
sentences.zh: 它完全浸透在英国文学之中，你知道的，对板球以及与之相关的一切都极为着迷。

sentences.en: And reading it now, it's kind of positive about Britain in a way that very few British people today are.
sentences.zh: 现在读这本书，你会觉得它对英国的肯定态度是当今极少数英国人所不具备的。

sentences.en: And I think that it kind of points to the way in which anti-imperialism paradoxically was something that was exported by the British as well as imperialism.
sentences.zh: 我认为这指出了这样一种方式：具有讽刺意味的是，反帝主义和帝国主义一样，也是由英国人输出的东西。

sentences.en: And even someone like Frantz Fanon, you know, who's in a way the kind of the great spokesman for anti-colonialism, born in and raised in the French Caribbean Empire.
sentences.zh: 甚至像法农这样的人，你知道，他在某种程度上可以说是反殖民主义的伟大代言人，出生并在法属加勒比帝国长大。

sentences.en: He is saturated in philosophical assumptions that derive from...
sentences.zh: 他身上充满了源自……的哲学假设。

sentences.en: Oh, Ho Chi Minh.
sentences.zh: 噢，胡志明。

sentences.en: Yeah, or Ho Chi Minh, yes.
sentences.zh: 对，或者胡志明，是的。

sentences.en: Ho Chi Minh worked as a chef, I believe, under Lescoffiers.
sentences.zh: 据我所知，胡志明曾在埃斯科菲耶手下当过厨师。

sentences.en: That's a subject for another podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 那是另一期播客的话题了。

sentences.en: So let's move on to another question, which is on this sort of ground, which is from Tom Shaw.
sentences.zh: 所以让我们继续讨论下一个问题，也是关于这方面的，由汤姆·肖提出。

sentences.en: Tom Shaw says,
sentences.zh: 汤姆·肖说，

sentences.en: Well, I, you know, to stick to Britain, I think that our attitudes to the Roman Empire, again, are incredibly paradoxical.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我，你知道的，就拿英国来说，我认为我们对罗马帝国的态度同样充满了矛盾。

sentences.en: Because for British people in the 19th and 20th century, who are they identifying with?
sentences.zh: 因为对于十九和二十世纪的英国人来说，他们认同的对象是谁？

sentences.en: Are they identifying with the Britons or are they identifying with the Romans?
sentences.zh: 他们认同的是布立吞人，还是罗马人？

sentences.en: So outside the Houses of Parliament, next to Westminster Bridge, you have a statue of Boudicca, whose name means victory.
sentences.zh: 所以在议会大厦外，威斯敏斯特桥旁，立着一座布狄卡的雕像，她的名字意为胜利。

sentences.en: So Victoria.
sentences.zh: 也就是维多利亚。

sentences.en: So she's an emblem of the British Queen, member of, you know, summoning up the idea that the Britons are destined to rule and to fight.
sentences.zh: 所以她是英国女王的象征，唤起了一种观念，即布立吞人注定要统治和战斗。

sentences.en: But of course, Boudicca is a rebel against imperial power.
sentences.zh: 但当然，布狄卡是帝国权力的反抗者。

sentences.en: And there is a sense as well that the British identify with the Romans.
sentences.zh: 而且人们也有一种感觉，即英国人认同罗马人。

sentences.en: And that kind of tortured, conflicted sense is, I think, still very much with us.
sentences.zh: 这种备受折磨、充满冲突感的心态，我认为至今仍然伴随着我们。

sentences.en: We're kind of conflated Boudicca and Britannia, haven't we?
sentences.zh: 我们把布狄卡和不列颠尼亚混为一谈了，对吧？

sentences.en: So the image of Britannia that used to be on the 50p, the sort of the Roman or Greek helmet and the shield and all that sort of stuff.
sentences.zh: 所以过去印在五十便士硬币上的不列颠尼亚形象，那种罗马或希腊头盔、盾牌以及诸如此类的东西。

sentences.en: In the public mind, I think they're kind of the same.
sentences.zh: 在公众心目中，我认为它们基本上是一回事。

sentences.en: They sort of merge into this sort of Elizabeth the First type, you know, this sort of feminine personification of Britain,
sentences.zh: 它们融合成了一种伊丽莎白一世风格的形象，你知道的，这种英国女性拟人化形象，

sentences.en: which is both fighting foreign imperialists and an imperialist in and of itself.
sentences.zh: 她既与外国帝国主义者战斗，其本身又是一个帝国主义者。

sentences.en: Well, but just to follow up on that, I think it's a commentary on the reality of Roman imperialism,
sentences.zh: 嗯，但接着这一点说，我认为这是对罗马帝国主义现实的一种讽刺，

sentences.en: that the first representation of Britannia shows her as a woman being raped by the Emperor Claudius.
sentences.zh: 那就是不列颠尼亚最初的形象是一个被克劳狄皇帝强奸的女性。

sentences.en: Oh, so that doesn't doesn't tend to feature on the coins.
sentences.zh: 哦，所以这通常不会出现在硬币上。

sentences.en: No, I wouldn't.
sentences.zh: 对，不会的。

sentences.en: Go on, you choose a question.
sentences.zh: 来吧，你来选一个问题。

sentences.en: Well, there's one about Christianity, which I suspect you don't want me to.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这里有一个关于基督教的问题，我猜你不会想让我选。

sentences.en: We'll skip over that one.
sentences.zh: 我们跳过那个吧。

sentences.en: Here's one from George Ellingham.
sentences.zh: 这里有一个来自乔治·埃灵顿的问题。

sentences.en: Do empires that intend to last aspire to become a single nation federal state, i.e. China and the Soviet Union, or is this a more modern nation?
sentences.zh: 那些想要持久的帝国，是否渴望成为一个单一民族的联邦国家，即中国和苏联，或者这是一种更现代的国家形态？

sentences.en: Oh, that's a good question.
sentences.zh: 哦，这是个好问题。

sentences.en: That is an excellent question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个极好的问题。

sentences.en: Do they aspire to that?
sentences.zh: 他们渴望那样做吗？

sentences.en: I think probably not at first, though you do get.
sentences.zh: 我想最初可能并非如此，尽管你确实会遇到这种情况。

sentences.en: So, for example, with Russia, you had you've had moments of kind of Russification, if that's a word.
sentences.zh: 所以，例如对俄罗斯来说，你曾有过那种俄罗斯化的时刻，如果可以这么说的话。

sentences.en: And the sort of tendency was to try and Russify provinces, let's say the Baltic states or Ukraine,
sentences.zh: 这种倾向是试图将各省俄罗斯化，比方说波罗的海国家或乌克兰，

sentences.en: and to see them as kind of Russia's little brothers and to eradicate kind of national differences.
sentences.zh: 把它们看作俄罗斯的小弟弟，并根除某种民族差异。

sentences.en: Though it's interesting with Russia, how, you know, Russia is still quite a sort of fragmented country.
sentences.zh: 不过有趣的是，就俄罗斯而言，你知道，俄罗斯仍然是一个相当碎片化的国家。

sentences.en: It's politically, you know, if you look at the map, the way it's structured, it still sort of follows old patterns.
sentences.zh: 在政治上，你知道，如果你看看地图，看它的结构方式，它仍然在某种程度上遵循着旧的模式。

sentences.en: And you have Tatarstan and so on, Kalmachia and the Caucasus.
sentences.zh: 你有鞑靼斯坦等等，卡尔梅克和高加索。

sentences.en: I mean, the Caucasus is a very good example of how you can't just impose a kind of imperial stamp and turn everybody into little Russians.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，高加索就是一个很好的例子，说明你不能只是强加一种帝国印记，把所有人都变成小俄罗斯人。

sentences.en: But Caucasus is mountainous.
sentences.zh: 但高加索是多山地区。

sentences.en: So that's kind of another fact, you know, that empires tend to reach geographical borders where.
sentences.zh: 所以这也是另一个事实，你知道，帝国往往会延伸到地理边界，在那里……

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that's absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 是的，我觉得这绝对正确。

sentences.en: And let's say China.
sentences.zh: 再比如中国。

sentences.en: I mean, China has limits.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，中国是有极限的。

sentences.en: You know, China can't go on expanding forever.
sentences.zh: 你知道，中国不可能永远扩张下去。

sentences.en: I think the Chinese recognize they had limits.
sentences.zh: 我认为中国认识到了他们有极限。

sentences.en: And with the peoples who were on the sort of margins of their empire, the Uyghurs are the obvious newsworthy example.
sentences.zh: 而对于那些处于其帝国边缘的人群，维吾尔人就是一个显而易见备受关注的例子。

sentences.en: They are, you know, they don't see themselves as Han Chinese.
sentences.zh: 他们，你知道，并不认为自己是汉族。

sentences.en: And hence the stories that you get in the media about camps and about indoctrination and all the rest of it.
sentences.zh: 因此，你在媒体上看到的关于集中营、关于洗脑以及其他种种的报道也就应运而生了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, yeah, I think, well, I think, George, empires may have that aspiration, but to realize it is a very different matter.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我想，乔治，帝国或许有那种渴望，但要实现它则是另一回事。

sentences.en: OK, so following that up with a question from Neil Connolly, when do we stop calling an empire an empire?
sentences.zh: 好的，那么接着尼尔·康纳利的一个问题，我们什么时候不再把一个帝国称之为帝国？

sentences.en: So that's an interesting.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个有趣的问题。

sentences.en: Much of Russia is a result of imperial conquest, yet we happily consider its territory to be part of the state.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯的大部分领土都是帝国征服的产物，然而我们却欣然将它的领土视为国家的一部分。

sentences.en: Likewise, the Western USA and Northern Ireland.
sentences.zh: 同样，美国西部和北爱尔兰也是如此。

sentences.en: So, actually, not just the Western USA, the whole of the USA.
sentences.zh: 所以，实际上，不仅仅是美国西部，而是整个美国。

sentences.en: I mean, the whole of the USA, the whole of America is an imperial project, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，整个美国，整个美洲都是一个帝国项目，不是吗？

sentences.en: It is, right.
sentences.zh: 确实是。

sentences.en: And I think it's very strange.
sentences.zh: 而且我觉得这非常奇怪。

sentences.en: You know, scholars have written books about American empire and American imperialism.
sentences.zh: 你知道，学者们写过很多关于美国帝国和美国帝国主义的书。

sentences.en: And Americans themselves resist it because, of course, their nation, their sort of founding myth is the sort of Star Wars myth of, you know,
sentences.zh: 而美国人自己却对此进行抵制，因为当然，他们的国家，他们某种意义上的建国神话，就像是《星球大战》里的神话，你知道的，

sentences.en: plucky rebels fighting off the evil galactic empire, which is us.
sentences.zh: 勇敢的起义军反抗邪恶的银河帝国，也就是我们。

sentences.en: And so they sort of deny their own imperial nature.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们某种程度上否认了自身的帝国本质。

sentences.en: But, of course, the United States is an empire.
sentences.zh: 但当然，美国就是一个帝国。

sentences.en: It has all the trappings of empire.
sentences.zh: 它具备帝国的一切特征。

sentences.en: It has subject peoples, which is to say the Native Americans in their reservations.
sentences.zh: 它有被统治的人民，也就是保留地里的美洲原住民。

sentences.en: It has colonies.
sentences.zh: 它有殖民地。

sentences.en: It has Puerto Rico and it had the Philippines.
sentences.zh: 它有波多黎各，过去还有菲律宾。

sentences.en: It has imperial conquest and stuff taken from Mexico.
sentences.zh: 它有帝国征服所得以及从墨西哥夺取的东西。

sentences.en: Stuff taken.
sentences.zh: 夺取的东西。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's got bases all over the world.
sentences.zh: 它在全世界都有军事基地。

sentences.en: It exerts influence in a way that, you know, if you were a Roman strategist in the sort of third century,
sentences.zh: 它施加影响的方式，你知道的，如果你是一个三世纪左右的罗马战略家，

sentences.en: thinking about your rivalry with the Persians or with the sort of the peoples to your north.
sentences.zh: 考虑你与波斯人或者你北方的那些部族之间的竞争。

sentences.en: And in Africa and so on.
sentences.zh: 还有在非洲等等地方。

sentences.en: And the way in which you play those off against each other and your client states and your buffer zones.
sentences.zh: 以及你在他们之间、在你的附属国和缓冲区之间进行纵横捭阖的方式。

sentences.en: And that's how American policymakers think.
sentences.zh: 这就是美国决策者的思维方式。

sentences.en: You know, that's what they study at West Point.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这就是他们在西点军校学习的内容。

sentences.en: That's what the people who are in the Council of Foreign Relations and all these things in Washington, D.C.,
sentences.zh: 这就是那些在华盛顿特区的外交关系委员会以及所有这些机构里任职的人，

sentences.en: they look back to Roman because they know that deep down that they are an empire as those previous states were too.
sentences.zh: 他们回顾罗马，因为他们内心深处知道，他们就像之前的那些国家一样，也是一个帝国。

sentences.en: OK, Dom, I've got the perfect follow up for you.
sentences.zh: 好吧，多姆，我为你准备了一个绝佳的后续问题。

sentences.en: That one is from Colonel Neal.
sentences.zh: 这个问题来自尼尔上校。

sentences.en: Might it be said that the empires of today exist digitally rather than nationally?
sentences.zh: 是否可以说，当今的帝国更多是以数字形式存在，而不是以国家形式存在？

sentences.en: Google, Amazon, Microsoft and, of course, Facebook, because as we're recording this, Facebook is in a kind of, you know,
sentences.zh: 谷歌、亚马逊、微软，当然还有脸书，因为在我们录制这期节目时，脸书正处于一种，你知道的，

sentences.en: gunboat diplomacy style standoff with the Australian government.
sentences.zh: 类似于炮舰外交的僵局中，与澳大利亚政府对峙。

sentences.en: That's a really interesting question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常有趣的问题。

sentences.en: Because we have had commercial, I mean, the East India Company is a classic example.
sentences.zh: 因为我们有过商业帝国，我是说，东印度公司就是一个典型的例子。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And the Dutch.
sentences.zh: 还有荷兰人。

sentences.en: Of a private, of a company.
sentences.zh: 关于一个私人公司，关于一家公司。

sentences.en: Yeah, the Dutch East India Company.
sentences.zh: 对，荷兰东印度公司。

sentences.en: So of companies that became, that became empires.
sentences.zh: 所以说有些公司成为了，成为了帝国。

sentences.en: But then they were sort of, it's interesting how they were then subsumed within the idea of a kind of traditional, I was about to say a national empire,
sentences.zh: 但有趣的是，它们后来又是如何被归入某种传统概念之中的，我本来想说传统帝国的概念，

sentences.en: if that's not a contradiction in terMs.
sentences.zh: 如果这不算自相矛盾的话。

sentences.en: But you know what I mean?
sentences.zh: 但你知道我的意思吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 知道。

sentences.en: The East India Company was basically taken over by the British state, or at least its possessions were.
sentences.zh: 东印度公司基本上被英国政府接管了，或者至少它的领地是这样的。

sentences.en: Will that happen?
sentences.zh: 这种情况会发生吗？

sentences.en: I mean, that Google had digitally.
sentences.zh: 我是说，谷歌在数字领域也是如此。

sentences.en: I mean, that's very hard to say, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这很难说，对吧？

sentences.en: Empires of the mind, I suppose.
sentences.zh: 我想，这就是精神上的帝国。

sentences.en: I remember I went to Silicon Valley and went on a tour around the kind of various campuses of the big sites.
sentences.zh: 我记得我去过硅谷，参观了那些大型科技公司的各个园区。

sentences.en: And I think it was Google.
sentences.zh: 我想那是谷歌。

sentences.en: They had a huge, great kind of sign with Google on it.
sentences.zh: 他们有一个巨大的、带有谷歌字样的招牌。

sentences.en: And then we went around and looked around the back and it was there on the back was some fallen company.
sentences.zh: 然后我们绕到后面去看，发现背面竟然是一家倒闭公司的招牌。

sentences.en: And it had obviously been, yes, it had obviously been recycled.
sentences.zh: 显然，是的，它显然被回收利用了。

sentences.en: And, you know, you imagine Google could afford a fresh, could afford a fresh sign, but it's obviously, yes.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，你会觉得谷歌完全买得起一块崭新的、全新的招牌，但这显然是刻意为之，是的。

sentences.en: So it must have been deliberate, a kind of trampling on the grave of the fallen empire, which is kind of magnificent.
sentences.zh: 所以这一定是有意为之，有点像是在践踏那个陨落帝国的坟墓，这某种程度上相当壮观。

sentences.en: Or something.
sentences.zh: 或者类似的事情。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Okay, here's one from Lucas Roth.
sentences.zh: 好的，这里有一个来自卢卡斯·罗斯的问题。

sentences.en: Were people living in empires?
sentences.zh: 生活在帝国里的人们，

sentences.en: I was hoping you were going to ask Lucas Roth.
sentences.zh: 我刚才就希望你会问卢卡斯·罗斯的问题。

sentences.en: Were people living in empires, living in empires, better off, in inverted commas, than people living outside the empire?
sentences.zh: 生活在帝国里的人们，比起生活在帝国之外的人们，是否“过得更好”——这里加了引号？

sentences.en: That is, you know, that takes us back to quite a lot of what we've been talking about.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，这把我们带回了我们一直在讨论的许多内容。

sentences.en: Well, it depends on your empire, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，这取决于你指的是哪个帝国，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, if you're living in the Belgian Congo,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你生活在比利时统治下的刚果，

sentences.en: I would say it's preferable to be living outside the borders of that particular territory because you don't want to have your hands cut off because you haven't collected enough rubber or whatever.
sentences.zh: 我认为生活在那个特定领土的边界之外会更好，因为你可不想因为没有收集到足够的橡胶或其他东西而被砍掉双手。

sentences.en: Were you better off to be in the Roman Empire than outside it or the Persian Empire than outside it, let's say?
sentences.zh: 比起生活在罗马帝国之外，生活在罗马帝国之内会不会更好？或者相比波斯帝国之外，生活在其中会更好？

sentences.en: I mean, my answer to that would probably be yes, because I think empire offered you, you know, if you were, I mean, obviously, if you're unfortunate, you know,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我对这个问题的回答可能倾向于“是”，因为我认为帝国为你提供了，你知道的，如果你——当然，如果你不幸的话，你知道，

sentences.en: things are pretty rough under empires.
sentences.zh: 在帝国统治下生活其实挺艰难的。

sentences.en: But if you're fortunate, if you're blessed by talent, for example, you have opportunities for advancement, for travel, for economic prosperity and so on,
sentences.zh: 但如果你很幸运，如果你的才华受到眷顾，例如，你有机会获得晋升、去各地旅行、享受经济繁荣等等，

sentences.en: that you probably wouldn't get if you were born in the sort of Germanic forests.
sentences.zh: 这些如果你出生在日耳曼森林里的话，大概是无法得到的。

sentences.en: Now, maybe that's just my prejudice talking to you.
sentences.zh: 现在，也许这只是我带有偏见在跟你说话。

sentences.en: What do you think?
sentences.zh: 你觉得呢？

sentences.en: Well, I think, again, we go that the great empires, the kind of transcontinental empires, China, Rome, so on, reach the natural limits, where basically it stops being worthwhile,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为，我们再次回到了那个规律：伟大的帝国，那种跨大陆的帝国——中国、罗马等等——达到了自然极限，征服所带来的开销和努力，

sentences.en: the expense and effort of conquering.
sentences.zh: 基本上变得不再值得。

sentences.en: So when the Romans reach the Rhine, basically, you know, Germany is not worth the effort.
sentences.zh: 所以当罗马人抵达莱茵河时，基本上，你知道的，日耳曼地区根本不值得付出努力。

sentences.en: It's not worth the effort of conquering.
sentences.zh: 不值得花心思去征服它。

sentences.en: And then you start to get the situation where actually it's people beyond the empire who want a bit of the wealth and the role that the various peoples who cross into the empire over the course of the fifth century is much debated.
sentences.zh: 然后你会发现这样一种情况：实际上是帝国之外的人渴望分一杯羹，而那些在五世纪期间跨入帝国境内的各族群所扮演的角色引发了诸多争论。

sentences.en: But clearly, I mean, they have a role to play and they're coming in because they want a bit of it in exactly the same way that, you know,
sentences.zh: 但很明显，我的意思是，他们确实扮演了一个角色，他们之所以进来，是因为他们想要分一杯羹，这正如，你知道的，

sentences.en: the Mongols famously invade and conquer China, that people outside want what empires have because it's richer.
sentences.zh: 蒙古人入侵并征服中国的著名历史一样，帝国之外的人想要帝国所拥有的东西，因为帝国更富庶。

sentences.en: And that sets up a kind of law of empire that you get in Herodotus, that you get in Tacitus, that you get in Ibn Khaldun, namely that empire softens people.
sentences.zh: 这就确立了一种帝国规律，你在希罗多德、塔西陀以及伊本·赫勒敦的著作中都能看到，即帝国会使人变得软弱。

sentences.en: And it's people outside empires who are left, you know, who are tough, who are hardy,
sentences.zh: 而留在帝国之外的人，你知道的，他们是坚强的、强悍的，

sentences.en: who have the virtues that the original imperial peoples had but have now lost because they've become, you know.
sentences.zh: 他们具备最初的帝国人民所拥有、但现在却因变得……而丧失的美德。

sentences.en: That's the sort of Spartan self-image, right?
sentences.zh: 这就是那种斯巴达式的自我形象，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Spartans versus the Persians or something.
sentences.zh: 斯巴达人对阵波斯人或者诸如此类。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So the Greeks, the Romans,
sentences.zh: 所以希腊人、罗马人、

sentences.en: the Arabs of the imperial age all have a kind of sense of themselves as a martial people who are better qualified for rule than the soft peoples that they conquer.
sentences.zh: 帝国时代的阿拉伯人都有一种自我认知，认为自己是一个崇尚武力的民族，比他们所征服的那些软弱的人更适合统治。

sentences.en: But in due course, the empires that they establish, you know, they become kind of silken and soft in turn and then become prey to the barbarians beyond the border.
sentences.zh: 但久而久之，他们建立的帝国，你知道的，反过来也会变得文弱娇惯，然后成为边境以外野蛮人的猎物。

sentences.en: And this is seen by all these writers writing very different periods as a kind of, you know, the rule of empire.
sentences.zh: 生活在截然不同时期的所有这些作家，都将此视为一种，你知道的，帝国的铁律。

sentences.en: And I would not be surprised.
sentences.zh: 对此我一点也不会感到意外。

sentences.en: I don't know enough about China to know whether the same thing is identified in China.
sentences.zh: 我对中国的了解还不够多，不知道中国是否也存在同样的现象。

sentences.en: I would guess it probably is.
sentences.zh: 我猜大概是有的。

sentences.en: But it's exactly what Americans say right now, that they've become distracted, self-indulgent.
sentences.zh: 但这正是美国人现在所说的，他们变得心猿意马、自我放纵。

sentences.en: You know, they're sunk in a kind of malaise of introspection and quarrelling and that they've lost the, you know,
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们陷入了一种内省和争吵不休的萎靡状态，他们已经失去了，你知道的，

sentences.en: the Spartan republican virtues of the founding fathers and all this sort of stuff or of the greatest generation.
sentences.zh: 国父们或最伟大一代的那种斯巴达式的共和美德以及所有这类东西。

sentences.en: So that trope is still there in the way that Americans talk about their empire.
sentences.zh: 所以这种修辞手法在美国人谈论他们的帝国时依然存在。

sentences.en: OK, I think I think we've I mean, we've barely scratched the surface.
sentences.zh: 好的，我想，我想我们——我们只是略窥皮毛。

sentences.en: We could talk about this for hours and hours, but it's a policy must be a policy of this podcast not to outstay our welcome.
sentences.zh: 我们可以没完没了地讨论这个话题，但本播客必须遵循一个原则，那就是不要逗留太久、招人嫌烦。

sentences.en: So just one last question for you, Dominic, from David Nicholson.
sentences.zh: 所以，多姆，请回答来自大卫·尼科尔森的最后一个问题。

sentences.en: Is there historical veracity to the claim that all empires day in the sun lasts around 200 years?
sentences.zh: 所有帝国的全盛时期都大约持续200年，这种说法在历史上有据可查吗？

sentences.en: And I ask that not just because the question in itself is interesting,
sentences.zh: 我问这个问题不仅是因为问题本身很有趣，

sentences.en: but because of the the idea that there might be kind of almost the equivalent of biological laws that govern empires.
sentences.zh: 还因为有一种观点认为，支配帝国的几乎存在着某种类似生物学规律的东西。

sentences.en: Can we, you know, can we say that empires do have a natural limit?
sentences.zh: 我们能不能，你知道的，我们能不能说帝国确实有其自然的极限？

sentences.en: What do you think?
sentences.zh: 你觉得呢？

sentences.en: I would say no.
sentences.zh: 我会说不。

sentences.en: And I don't think that 200 years works at all.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为200年的说法根本站不住脚。

sentences.en: And I don't think there is a limit.
sentences.zh: 我也认为并不存在什么极限。

sentences.en: So China, we had a whole podcast on China and China is the standing rebuke to that.
sentences.zh: 比如中国，我们曾专门做过一期关于中国的播客，中国就是对这种说法的最好反驳。

sentences.en: Now, I know there was this discussion about how is China?
sentences.zh: 现在，我知道曾有过这样的讨论：中国究竟是什么？

sentences.en: Has it always been one thing or has it been a succession of things on the same space?
sentences.zh: 它一直是一个统一的实体，还是同一片土地上一系列先后更替的事物？

sentences.en: But I think that it had the fact that it has inhabited the same space suggests continuity and suggests that you can keep it up.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，它一直在同一片土地上延续，这本身就说明了延续性，也表明你可以将其维持下去。

sentences.en: I mean, if you take some of the empires that people often forget about, we mentioned the Ottoman Empire or its predecessor, the Eastern Roman Empire,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你看看人们经常遗忘的一些帝国，我们提到了奥斯曼帝国或它的前身东罗马帝国，

sentences.en: which we now call the Byzantine Empire.
sentences.zh: 也就是我们现在所称的拜占庭帝国。

sentences.en: We tell the story of Rome and we say, well, then the Rome fell in 476.
sentences.zh: 我们讲述罗马的故事时会说，嗯，然后罗马在476年灭亡了。

sentences.en: And then basically there was a successor state in the East, but no one cares about that.
sentences.zh: 然后基本上东方出现了一个继承国，但没有人关心那个。

sentences.en: And it kind of went away.
sentences.zh: 它似乎就那样消失了。

sentences.en: And but that lasted a thousand years.
sentences.zh: 但是，那个帝国持续了一千年。

sentences.en: And it was a remarkably resilient and successful state attacked by lots of different predators and would-be conquerors.
sentences.zh: 它是一个极其具有韧性和成功的国家，遭受了许多不同掠夺者和潜在征服者的攻击。

sentences.en: And it lasted a very long time.
sentences.zh: 而且它存续了非常长的时间。

sentences.en: The Ottoman Empire lasted longer than the British Empire, the French Empire or whatever.
sentences.zh: 奥斯曼帝国的存续时间比大英帝国、法郎士帝国等等都要长。

sentences.en: So I think empires can last for centuries.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为帝国可以持续几个世纪。

sentences.en: And I don't think there is actually a, you know, the example of China or indeed Russia suggests that there isn't necessarily always this kind of sense of entropy.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为实际上并不存在——你知道的，中国甚至俄罗斯的例子表明，并不一定总是存在这种熵增的趋势。

sentences.en: You know, you don't have to fall apart.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你并不一定会分崩离析。

sentences.en: There is no biological.
sentences.zh: 根本没有什么生物学规律。

sentences.en: There is a point at which you can't expand.
sentences.zh: 确实存在一个无法继续扩张的节点。

sentences.en: I think that is certainly true.
sentences.zh: 我认为这绝对是真的。

sentences.en: Although maybe that law about expansion only applied in a pre-digital age because of transport and communications and so on.
sentences.zh: 尽管关于扩张的那个规律可能只适用于前数字时代，因为当时受限于交通和通信等等。

sentences.en: Maybe, you know, the chance of a really big empire is there in the 21st or 22nd century.
sentences.zh: 也许，你知道的，真正建立超级大帝国的机会在21世纪或22世纪是存在的。

sentences.en: What do you think?
sentences.zh: 你觉得呢？

sentences.en: I don't know what the future holds.
sentences.zh: 我不知道未来会怎样。

sentences.en: Profound words.
sentences.zh: 真是意味深长的话。

sentences.en: I know, I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道，我知道。

sentences.en: And I say that because you're right,
sentences.zh: 我这么说是因为你说得对，

sentences.en: that I don't know whether the opportunities presented by technology will facilitate the emergence of new ways of structuring societies and different hierarchies and things like that.
sentences.zh: 我不知道技术带来的机遇是否会促进新社会结构、不同等级制度以及诸如此类事物的涌现。

sentences.en: I mean, we haven't really talked about the role that technology plays in the emergence of empires.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们还没有真正讨论过技术在帝国崛起中所起的作用。

sentences.en: And that may be, you know, something for a future podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 这或许，你知道的，会成为未来某期播客的主题。

sentences.en: So I don't know.
sentences.zh: 所以我不知道。

sentences.en: I mean, I'm looking at China and the incredible skill with which it's utilising technology to, you know, entrench its rule over the kind of peripheral regions.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我看到中国正以惊人的技巧利用技术来，你知道的，巩固其对周边地区的统治。

sentences.en: I don't see the Uyghurs breaking free of Chinese imperial rule any time soon.
sentences.zh: 我看不出维吾尔人会在短时间内摆脱中国帝国的统治而获得自由。

sentences.en: So I wouldn't be able to answer that, really.
sentences.zh: 所以，我真的无法回答这个问题。

sentences.en: Here's a forward-looking thought, though.
sentences.zh: 不过，这里有一个面向未来的思考。

sentences.en: We talked about Europe earlier and about the failure of a single state to dominate the European sort of peninsula after the fall of the Western Roman Empire.
sentences.zh: 我们之前谈到了欧洲，以及西罗马帝国灭亡后，单一国家未能主宰欧洲半岛的现象。

sentences.en: Surely the chance now, you know, in the next hundred years or so, I mean, the dream of European enthusiasts is that there will be a single state.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，现在机会来了，你知道的，在接下来的一百年左右里，欧洲一体化热心者的梦想就是建立一个单一国家。

sentences.en: The European Union will become this empire in all but name.
sentences.zh: 欧盟将名副其实地成为这样一个帝国。

sentences.en: So the idea, to me,
sentences.zh: 所以在我看来，

sentences.en: the idea that the age of empires is behind us or that empires indeed have this sort of inbuilt limit or there are places that are naturally resistant to empires,
sentences.zh: 帝国时代已经过去，或者帝国确实有这种内置极限，又或者有些地方天生抗拒帝国的想法，

sentences.en: I don't really buy any of that.
sentences.zh: 这些我其实都不买账。

sentences.en: Well, that's a cheery name on which to end.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这是一个令人振奋的结束语。

sentences.en: Well, it depends if you like empires.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这取决于你是否喜欢帝国。

sentences.en: On which to end.
sentences.zh: 以此作为结束。

sentences.en: And I think also, you know, what we've realised from this discussion is that there's fruit for large numbers of subsequent podcasts.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，你知道的，我们从这次讨论中意识到的是，这为后续的大量播客提供了丰富的素材。

sentences.en: We've done about 4% of the questions, which is pretty straightforward in our own standards.
sentences.zh: 我们只回答了大约4%的问题，按照我们自己的标准，这已经相当直接了。

sentences.en: Many apologies there.
sentences.zh: 在此深表歉意。

sentences.en: But I think this is a subject definitely to come back to, perhaps with a slightly narrower focus.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这个主题绝对值得再次探讨，也许可以将焦点稍微收窄一些。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So I have a very nicely written conclusion here by the producer, which I want to read because it conjures up to me a very nice image.
sentences.zh: 所以这里有一段制作人写得非常精彩的结语，我想读一下，因为它在我的脑海中唤起了一个非常美好的画面。

sentences.en: The empire has fallen.
sentences.zh: 帝国已经陷落。

sentences.en: Tom Holland has been chased out by angry locals.
sentences.zh: 汤姆·霍兰德已被愤怒的当地人赶跑。

sentences.en: And the podcast has been returned to its rightful ruler, me.
sentences.zh: 而播客已经回到了其合法的统治者——我——的手中。

sentences.en: We're back on Thursday with historian and TV presenter Susie Lipscomb as we are delving into the dark world of witches and witchcraft.
sentences.zh: 我们在周四回归，届时历史学家兼电视节目主持人苏西·利普斯科姆将同我们一起深入探讨巫师与巫术的黑暗世界。

sentences.en: Until then, thanks for listening.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，感谢收听。

sentences.en: See you next time.
sentences.zh: 我们下期再见。

sentences.zh: 感谢收听《The Rest is History》。
